title: PTE Writing: Summarize Written Text & Essay
summary: The two PTE writing tasks — a one-sentence summary and a 200–300 word essay — and the exact rules the AI checks.

nodes.label: Form rules
nodes.note: Word count & one-sentence rule are scored

nodes.label: Grammar + spelling
nodes.note: Accuracy counts heavily for the AI

chunks.heading: Summarize Written Text — exactly one sentence
chunks.body: Read a passage and write a **single sentence of no more than 75 words** that captures its main point. The **one-sentence rule is strict**: use a full stop anywhere in the middle and you can lose the form mark entirely. It scores **reading and writing** together.
chunks.realExample: Combine ideas with linkers instead of full stops: 'Although X, the passage argues that Y, because Z.' One long, grammatical sentence — comma and 'because', never a period until the end.
chunks.memoryHook: One sentence, one full stop, ≤75 words. A second full stop = zero for form.

chunks.heading: Write Essay — 200 to 300 words, argue clearly
chunks.body: Write a **200–300 word** argumentative essay responding to a prompt. Stay **inside the word range** (too short or too long is penalised), take a **clear position**, and organise it into intro → body paragraphs → conclusion.
chunks.realExample: A safe, AI-friendly shape: intro (paraphrase + your position), two body paragraphs (each one reason + one example), a short conclusion restating the position. ~250 words, every time.
chunks.memoryHook: 250 words, 4 paragraphs, one clear position. Stay in the 200–300 lane.

chunks.heading: The AI rewards correctness over flair
chunks.body: Machine scoring weighs **grammar, spelling, vocabulary range and structure**. Clean, correct sentences beat ambitious ones with errors. **Leave 30 seconds to proofread** for typos and subject–verb agreement — cheap points the AI notices.
chunks.realExample: 'The government should to invest' loses marks a human might forgive; the AI won't. A quick reread catches exactly these slips.
chunks.memoryHook: Correct beats clever. Always leave 30 seconds to proofread.

chunks.heading: Templates help — but fill them with real content
chunks.body: A memorised **essay skeleton** keeps you fast and organised, but the AI scores **relevance to the prompt** too — so your reasons and examples must actually address the question, not just fill the template.
chunks.realExample: If the prompt is about remote work, a generic 'technology has changed our lives' intro scores worse than one that names the actual topic in the first sentence.
chunks.memoryHook: Template for the frame, real content for the marks. Name the topic early.

recall.q: What is the strict form rule for Summarize Written Text?
recall.a: It must be one single sentence of no more than 75 words — a second full stop can cost you the form mark.

recall.q: Which two skills does Summarize Written Text score?
What is the word range for the PTE essay, and why does it matter?
recall.a: 200–300 words; going under or over the range is penalised.

recall.q: What does the AI weigh most in PTE writing?
recall.a: Grammar, spelling, vocabulary range and structure — correctness over ambitious but error-prone writing.

recall.q: Why must your essay name the actual topic early?
recall.a: The AI also scores relevance to the prompt, so a generic template intro scores worse than one that addresses the question.
